verdicts.reason: A scatters the badges: TASTINGS sits alone top-left above the logo and ALL AGES top-right. FREE ENTRY is drawn as large as the RSVP CTA, all the copy is crammed into one small centred stack, SOLSTICE PRESENTS ends up below its own content, and a red missing-asset box is visible. B has a clear, dominant headline with the date and pills grouped beneath it, but RSVP Free is demoted to a pill the same size as the tag badges, the event details are stranded at the far left away from the date, SOLSTICE PRESENTS is tiny, and a red placeholder chip sits next to TASTINGS.

A shows a large, unrendered 'missing asset partner' placeholder with red text in the middle of the button stack, the logo is jammed against the right edge, and the pills (ALL AGES, FREE ENTRY, TASTINGS, RSVP) are scattered with no grid; the copy is small and the details text is tiny. B is a coherent centred banner with a strong headline, though the CTA has been reduced to a badge-sized pill, the time and place are split off to the left, and a small placeholder chip remains.

A has a dominant headline, the date and pills grouped together, and the subtitle on the right, but the RSVP CTA is no bigger than the badges, the details are separated at the far left, and a small red placeholder is visible. B lets a 'missing asset' placeholder with garbled text collide between the copy and the buttons, ALL AGES floats at top-left over the logo area, FREE ENTRY competes in size with RSVP, and the copy stack is cramped, with tiny reserve and presents lines.

A is the same coherent layout as above (strong headline, grouped pills), with flaws: the CTA is reduced to a badge, the details are split to the left, and a small placeholder chip is visible. In B the missing-asset placeholder overlaps the logo, so the brand mark is damaged. The headline is small, the left copy block runs against the edge, the product image floats in dead space in the middle, and RSVP Free is just one of four equal pills in a 2x2 grid.
